knowledge_units.context_summary: The text defines classes C_m,j as partitions of integers n >= k based on their 2-adic valuation of Stirling numbers S(n, k). It introduces the concept of m-level, where classes are split into two modulo 2^m. The main conjecture states that the first level with constant classes is m_0 - 1, where 2^(m_0-1) < k <= 2^m_0, and that subsequent levels maintain a constant number of classes.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text derives explicit formulas and 2-adic valuations for Stirling numbers of the second kind, S(n, 3) and S(n, 4). It proves that S(n, 3) is odd when n is odd and S(n, 3)/2 is odd when n is even, using recurrence relations and the ultrametric inequality. It also establishes that S(n, 4) is odd when n is even and even when n is odd.
